title: Current ES 8.8 regional exceptions differ from canonical AI mapping
problem: Current 8.8 tables have no named Security AI Assistant exception for Milan or São Paulo, while canonical esEssentials/esPremier/esCloudConnect assistantExcluded retains both. This is a candidate mapping discrepancy, not proof of feature rollout or grounds to remove qualifiers without reconciling the assistant runtime and full dependency chain. UAE AWS-services-disrupted row remains in Premier. No CMP GovCloud inference.

exclusions: No feature rollout, entitlement, runtime placement or customer authorization is established.

scopeComparison: Exact current 8.8 regional tables versus the existing canonical assistantExcluded mappings; historical 8.7 and feature runtime exclusions remain separate.

impact.customerScenario: Planning ES AI capability region eligibility.
impact.consequence: Canonical exclusions may overstate current table restrictions, but removing them before feature/runtime reconciliation could overstate availability.

confidence.rationale: Direct current regional table comparison establishes a mapping discrepancy; feature support remains unresolved.

lifecycle.reason: Current canonical mapping requires reconciliation with the exact regional table and feature runtime scope.

evidence.section: Complete Essentials, Premier and Cloud Connect tables; GCP/Azure availability; assistant compatibility
evidence.statement: Essentials lists Calgary, Stockholm and both GovCloud regions as AI Assistant/Agentic SOC exceptions. Premier lists Calgary and GovCloud exceptions; Montréal has no named exception. Cloud Connect lists Montréal assistant exception and no Calgary exception. Cloud GCP/Azure permits ES and SOAR only with SOAR unavailable in GCP US West.

documentRevision.qualification: Direct public response digest; publisher revision is not inferred.
